content.text:
No, it isn't safe if your variable names (like `--color-*`) can collide with variables on your users' sites. Tailwind v4 has a prefix option that puts the protection back.

- Import Tailwind with `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);`. Keep defining your theme variables without the prefix, for example `--font-display` inside `@theme`. The generated CSS variables then include the prefix, for example `--tw-font-display`, "to avoid conflicts with any existing variables in your project." (`src/docs/upgrade-guide.mdx`, section "Using a prefix")
- The prefix also changes class names. They become variant-style and always come first, as in `tw:flex`. Built-in utilities like `rounded-lg` still work, but your users' markup would need to use the prefixed form. This is a side effect of the same option.

I didn't search `theme.mdx` for other ways to reduce collisions, such as removing unused defaults with `--color-*: initial`. The graphify query the project asks for was blocked by a permission denial, so I read the docs with grep directly.
